Goldens. In the CLI byte sweep, 7 of 12,550 goldens change bytes and none panic. edge_seq_title_with_variables is a %date() clock artefact: the two runs straddled a second, and a rerun gives identical bytes. splines_multilevel_inheritance goes from DIFF 1 to MATCH, and splines_self_reference_ortho from DIFF 10 to DIFF 1. On the ER goldens, er_financial (45/45), er_healthcare (54/54) and er_hr (158/158) are neutral by count, and er_ecommerce is worse (99 to 100). er_hr's 'manages' self-loop label moves from (344.82, 258.52) to (400.69, 282.23) against Java's (390.03, 308.82), which is closer. golden_no_oracle passes on both trees: 70 failures at base, 69 at the tip; the only name change is the gain rendering/splines/splines_multilevel_inheritance, consistent with the 11,182/11,251 lock and the doc pins (doc_claims passes). golden_pairs, the oracle-assisted strict tier, fails identically on both trees in this environment: 10,497 passed, 754 failed, the same names, and the same maximum deviation for the ER park candidates (ecommerce 34.0, hr 17.41).

Cause of the er_ecommerce worsening. The packet sends every ortho center label as xlabel, which is a faithful port of SvekEdge.appendLine 425-431 (useXLabelInsteadOfLabel || NO_LEFT_RIGHT_AND_XLABEL || DotSplines.ORTHO, self-loops included). For Category ||--o{ Category : "parent of", though, Rust's pre-existing self-loop route is a Bezier loop on the RIGHT of Category: 'M994.59,514.66 C1014.41,517.76 1021.2,529.73 1021.2,553.06 ...'. Java routes it orthogonally on the LEFT: 'M904,487.65 ... 816.38,491.62 ... 816.38,612.62 ... 931.4,612.62'. Graphviz puts the xlabel beside Rust's route, at x 1027.19, against Java's 753.38 and base's synthesized 936.53, and that label sets the canvas. Special-casing self-loops to dodge this would be un-Java. The fix is the ortho self-loop route itself, or explicit parent sign-off on this one golden.

Challenge 1, escape handling. relationship_label_display is a line-for-line port of Display.getWithNewlines 258-341: raw mode at [[, <math> and <latex>; \\n, \\r and \\l break the line, and \\r and \\l set natural alignment (last wins); \\t becomes a tab; \\\\ becomes one backslash; any other pair is kept; a trailing lone backslash is kept; %n() stays literal because SPECIAL_NEWLINE_IN_DISPLAY_CLASS is false. DA bears this out: four_then_break, three_bs, tab_then_align, quant_esc, roles_align, stereo_nl, stereo_lit, mono_split, url_label_nl, url_multibar_nl and tip_bar_nl all go from DIFF to MATCH, and unknown_esc and tilde_quant were already MATCH. Not ported: Jaws BLOCK_E1_BREAKLINE (U+E103, which splits even in raw mode), REAL_TABULATION, REAL_BACKSLASH, the NEWLINE_LEFT/RIGHT_ALIGN marks, INVISIBLE_QUOTE (dropped) and BackSlash.hiddenNewLine. Rust's port treats only a real '\n' as BLOCK_E1_NEWLINE. No DA input exercises these. Residues outside the escape port: code_keep and code_split, where Rust applies <code> Creole and Java draws it literally (base fails too); mono_keep is DIFF 1 on canvas width (132 against 123).

Challenge 2, the bar. relationship_link_parts is not Java's UrlBuilder regex. It takes the first {...} anywhere as the tooltip and splits the label at the first plain space. It has none of the five-alternative order (QUOTED, ONLY_TOOLTIP, ONLY_TOOLTIP_AND_LABEL, LINK_TOOLTIP_NOLABEL, LINK_WITH_OPTIONAL...), no quote stripping (Url constructor), no [%s] (tab) or leading-whitespace rule, and no rejection of brackets. Held-out consequences in the packet's new direct-emit path: url_quoted_bar emits href '"https://ledger.example/a|b"' with the quotes kept (DIFF 13 to 2), and url_brace_nl takes 'extra' as the tooltip and truncates the label 'word{extra}' to 'word' (DIFF 11 to 5). The maker's claim that a bar 'is drawn as Java draws it' holds only for multi-line link labels. Single-line [[url|x]] still goes through the shared Creole URL parser, which splits on the first bar (creole.rs:426 and :1228). The same split happens in notes and class bodies on both binaries. url_bar_only (DIFF 3 to 4), url_bar_label (2 to 4; canvas 104 at base, 117 at the tip, 105 in Java) and url_brace_in_label (3 to 4) rise in strict count because the packet's Java-correct parser masking (protect_creole_links) now delivers the URL to that pre-existing parser. Base drew a stray ']' and no link. I attribute these to creole.rs, not to the packet. url_two (11 to 7), url_open (4 to 4, unclosed [[ stays text) and url_tip_only (10 to 10) are unchanged or improved.

Challenge 3, ortho. The xlabel skip is exactly 'route was rewritten': normalize_ortho_er_vertical_route returns true only for DoubleLine to CircleCrowFoot with four points sharing x (±0.01), and only then is edge.label cleared and the synthesizer run (render/class.rs synthesize_ortho_edge_labels). ORTHO_XLABEL_VERTICAL_INSET (5.0) and ORTHO_ER_VERTICAL_ROUTE_DELTAS are unchanged, and the diff adds no geometry constant. The only new numeric literal is TextBlockArrow2's .80. DA LR results: ext, comp, agg, dep and real (<|..), flat dl_cc and cc_dl, nest dl_cc and cc_dl, ortho_esc_lr and ortho_note all go from DIFF to MATCH. DA TB results: ext, comp, agg, dep and real are DIFF 18 at base and DIFF 3 at the tip; all three label lines are 43 px left of Java (x 48.95 against 91.95 at the same y) inside nested packages, a pre-existing Graphviz xlabel x-placement divergence. flat_dl_cc_tb (24 to 10) and nest_dl_cc_tb (24 to 11) leave the vertical synthesizer residue (labels 0.1 px high), which the packet was told not to refit. Self-links: self_dl_cc_tb goes from 18 to 1 (canvas height 99 against 114) and self_dl_cc_lr from 18 to 17 (labels within 0.1 px, canvas 135 against 145). #--, x-- and +-- links are dropped entirely by the parser on both binaries.

TextBlockArrow2 misses Java's integer division. Java computes final int triSize = (int)(size*.80) and then translates and samples with triSize / 2 in int arithmetic. link_arrow_polygon_points uses triangle / 2.0. Whenever triSize is odd, the radius and the translate are 0.5 too large: font sizes 7, 9, 12, 14 and 17 (triSize 5, 7, 9, 11, 13). That is exactly the CO residue at g4k_magic_sz7 and g4k_magic_sz9 (DIFF 1 each at the tip: Java tip x 43.86, Rust 44.36). This is not a loss, since base is DIFF 11 on both cases.

proposed_targets: Creole [[...]] links are parsed by UrlBuilder.getUrl's five alternatives in order, in link labels, notes and class bodies (creole.rs:426, :1228 and render/class.rs relationship_link_parts): a bar stays in the URL, quotes are stripped (Url constructor), a {tooltip} binds only after the link, the label needs [%s], and brackets reject. A line ending in a single backslash joins the next line before @start/@end detection, as in Java, so a continuation that swallows @enduml gives Java's 'No valid @start/@end found' (exit 100). Witness: DA g4r2_trail_bs.
... in link labels is drawn as Java draws it (literal, not Creole). Witnesses: DA g4r2_code_keep and g4r2_code_split.
